excerpts.text: Therefore, the notion of peremptory norms became part of positive international law through the two articles 53 and 64 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969.

3. International Law Commission’s work on the codiﬁcation of unilateral acts and the matter of jus cogens The concept of jus cogens has become a preventive weapon in International Law because in practice, there are no known examples of treaties that derogate from such rules. In other words, the international practice did not witness any examples of treaties invalidity as a result of their conﬂict with a peremptory norm. It appears that States have attempted to circumvent the content of jus cogens by resorting to unilateral acts to depart from REPS 4,3 186 peremptory norms rather than treaties, as unilateral acts have remained for a considerable period beyond the umbrella of restraint imposed by jus cogens, at least in practice (Diaconu, 2016).
